title: Regeneration
definition: Regeneration is the work of God by which He gives new spiritual life to those who were dead in sin.
summary: Regeneration is the new birth by which God makes sinners spiritually alive.
christFocus: Jesus taught that sinners must be born again, and through Him the Spirit gives new life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Regeneration is God's life-giving work in the heart. Sinners are not merely spiritually weak; Scripture describes them as dead in sin. They need new birth, not just moral improvement.

In regeneration, God gives a new heart and new life by the Holy Spirit. This work enables repentance, faith, love for God, and a new direction of life.

Regeneration shows that salvation begins with God's mercy. The believer's new life is not self-created; it is the gracious work of God who makes the dead alive in Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people think Christianity is only behavior change or religious commitment. Regeneration matters because it teaches that people need inward new life from God, not merely outward reform.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask God to make your heart alive to Him and thank Him for every evidence of new life. Do not settle for outward religion. Pursue the practices that nourish spiritual life: Scripture, prayer, fellowship, repentance, and obedience.
